checks: The weights 1/s, 1, ε/s give identically zero weighted margin for x, the oblique margin and the lower frame margin. This proves whole-space cover. The inequalities x≤0, x≥εy+s/4 and y≥−B force the unique simultaneous nonpositive point (0,−B), where the maximum is zero.
Since B=s/(4ε)>1, all frame margins miss the square. The two principal normals have unit length and the moving oblique boundary stays in (−1,1) for every source y and ε≤1/8.
Integrating the oblique interval length gives 2(1+s/4). Integrating its squared length divided by 2s over y gives ((1+s/4)²+ε²/3)/s. The mass ratio is strictly below 2/3 since s<4/3.
The first hinge is one and the oblique hinge tends to 25/16. Independent arithmetic confirms 41/16 and the strict budget. This matches b488285aaeabe80d §7 and concerns feasible covers.

overlap.comparison: That example concerns width-normalized optimum degeneration on interval fibers. It does not have a fixed square source, bounded ordinary hinges, and a unique escaping framed minimax contact.
The earlier whole-line regression example has a fixed contact and varying interval-source positions, while this example fixes the source and sends its contact to infinity.

readability: The hypotheses and the proof use the same scope.
review_method: Independent cold read of the exact frozen candidate, followed by source, hypothesis, overlap and arithmetic checks.
summary: The six explicit margins give strictly feasible framed whole-space covers with bounded source hinges and a unique divergent contact.
